feature: A long edit opens without freezing
summary: The 6, 20 and 60 minute reference edits now open with no main thread pause over 100 ms, as the first window of a run. Worst pauses at the start of this task were 171, 185 and 230 ms; at the start of the whole task (2026-11-12) 2.9 s, 14 s and 135 s.
setup: Photonz Dev, release Next, no flag changed from its default. Scripts/perf/reference-edit.sh 6, 20 or 60 writes and opens the project.

try.do: Run Scripts/perf/reference-edit.sh 20 and watch the window appear.
Click a clip on V1 as soon as the window appears.
Run Scripts/perf/reference-edit.sh 60 and click the ruler at 30:00 the moment it shows.
Open a large screenshot with File > Open and check the window comes up already sized to it.
Open a 6 minute edit (reference-edit.sh 6), press Space to play and Space to stop.

evaluate: Does each window appear in one go, already sized and drawn, with no empty frame or jump in size?
Does the tool bar under the picture simply sit there when the window shows, rather than sliding up?
On the 20 minute edit, do the quiet tracks (V2 to V4, titles) look the same as before now that their clips are painted rather than built one by one?
Does the first click land straight away on all three edits?
rough: Worst main thread pass while opening, first window of a run, walk markers down (ms, before -> after): 6 min 171 -> 72 to 80; 20 min 185 -> 71 to 78; 60 min 228-239 -> 93 to 97. A second window opened beside one already open: 20 min 105 -> 58 to 76. A 12 megapixel picture: 150 -> 64.

What changed: a window opening a file is made and laid out hidden first, and the file lands in it a turn later, so making the window and building the document are two passes instead of one; it is shown, as before, once it has been sized to what it holds. A video opening into Edit now brings the ruler and tool bar a pass after the window draws (no slide), and an edit of 100 clips or more paints its quiet tracks' clips instead of building a bar for each (was 200).

The timeline takes the keyboard as the document lands, not when its key catcher joins the window: changed there, it set off a whole update of the window inside SwiftUI's own, about 36 ms of the 20 minute edit's opening.

Ztabby, the window switcher on this Mac, still reads each new window's accessibility tree a moment after it opens; that read is now 75 to 80 ms on the 20 minute edit (was about 92) and it is the slowest pass left on the 6 minute one.
The window opening shared code, so Current gets the same opening; nothing on screen differs once the window is open. No mock covers opening speed.
Guards: an-hour-long-edit-opens-without-a-freeze-walk now fails at 150 ms (was 300), and the new a-twenty-minute-edit-opens-without-a-pause-walk at 120 ms.
